The '''1988–89 DDR-Oberliga''' was the 40th season of the [[DDR-Oberliga]], the first tier of [[East German football league system|league football]] in [[East Germany]].

The league was contested by fourteen teams. [[Dynamo Dresden]] won the championship, the club's seventh out of eight East German championships.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrchamp.html |title= East Germany - List of Champions |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 26 January 2016}}</ref><ref name="Meister" >{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/historie/ddr-fussball/meister/ |title= DDR-Meister |website=dfb.de |publisher=[[German Football Association]] |access-date= 26 January 2016|language=de|trans-title= East German champions}}</ref>

[[Torsten Gütschow]] of Dynamo Dresden was the league's top scorer with 17 goals,<ref name="Goal" >{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/torschuetzenkoenige/gdr-oberliga/ |title= DDDR » Oberliga » Torschützenkönige  |website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 25 January 2016|language=de|trans-title=DDR-Oberliga top scorers }}</ref> while [[Andreas Trautmann]] of Dynamo Dresden took out the seasons [[Footballer of the Year in Germany|East German Footballer of the year]] award.<ref>''fuwo'', page: 92</ref>

On the strength of the 1988–89 title Dynamo Dresden qualified for the [[1989–90 European Cup]] where the club was knocked out by [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] in the first round. Second-placed club [[BFC Dynamo]] qualified for the [[1989–90 European Cup Winners' Cup]] as the seasons [[FDGB-Pokal]] winners and was knocked out by [[AS Monaco]] in the second round. Third-placed [[Chemnitzer FC|FC Karl-Marx-Stadt]] qualified for the [[1989–90 UEFA Cup]] where it was knocked out by [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the third round while fourth-placed [[F.C. Hansa Rostock]] lost to [[FC Baník Ostrava]] in the first round.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/ec/ec198990.html |title= European Competitions 1989–90 |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 26 January 2016}}</ref>

==Table==									
The 1988–89 season saw two newly promoted clubs, [[FC Energie Cottbus|BSG Energie Cottbus]] and [[FSV Zwickau|BSG Sachsenring Zwickau]].<ref name="Ddr" >{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesd/ddrhist.html |title= East Germany 1946-1990 |website= [[RSSSF]] |access-date= 26 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.weltfussball.de/spielplan/gdr-oberliga-1988-1989-spieltag/26/ |title= DDR-Oberliga 1988–89|website= Weltfussball.de |access-date= 26 January 2016|language=de}}</ref>
